cameras.name: Cameras
cameras.description: Live camera feeds via go2rtc and UniFi Protect

versions.changelog: Transparent poster on replay videos: no play triangle while a scrub loads (2.7.0b3) (#92)

Relay go2rtc and talk through the app with guest checks (2.7.0b2) (#91)

* Relay go2rtc and talk through the app with guest checks (2.7.0b2)

Browsers no longer talk to go2rtc or the echo canceller directly:
- /cameras/api/ws?src=<stream> is a websocket on the app's own origin.
  It checks policy.can_view for the requesting user and relays to
  go2rtc's /api/ws on loopback.
- /api/talk?src=<token>: talk_prepare (which already checks can_talk)
  hands out a single-use, 30 s token. The kiosk connects with it to the
  app's own port; the app redeems it and relays to aec (or go2rtc)
  /api/talk.
- /cameras/go2rtc/video-stream.js (and video-rtc.js) are served by the
  app from go2rtc, so the page needs no go2rtc port.

This prepares the supervisor to bind go2rtc and aec to 127.0.0.1.

Requires bdh-sdk 0.42 (websocket routes, wsrelay).


* Share the live server's DB connection with the test websocket front


---------

Explicit guest rules: per-NVR/camera visibility, talk, PTZ, events window (#90)

Replace the hardcoded "guests see only the first NVR" rules with a Guests
settings page and one policy module (cameras/policy.py) used by every
endpoint serving camera data. Pop-ups get an Everyone / Only when signed in
audience, sent as admins_only alerts (bdh-sdk 0.41). Version 2.7.0b1.

Echo cancellation via the aec companion (2.6.0b16) (#89)

Declare the supervisor's aec companion and read BDH_AEC_URL instead of a
hand-entered setting, so every hub that installs cameras gets it.

Echo cancellation for doorbell talkback (beta) (#88)

Optional bdh-aec sidecar URL (Settings -> Advanced). When set, two-way
cameras play full-screen/popup audio from <stream>_aec (Protect video +
echo-cancelled mic from the sidecar) and kiosk talk goes through the
sidecar's /api/talk so it has the echo reference.

Pop-up: send alert hold/hangup in the embed-host format (2.6.0b14) (#87)

The hub loads alert pop-ups in /apps/cameras/_bare/, so the pop-up's parent
is the bare page, not the alert overlay; the old {bdhAlert} message was
dropped there and the pop-up closed mid-conversation. Send
{bdh:1, type:'alert', cmd}, which the hub's embed-host relays to the overlay
(BlackDiamondHub #372).

Pop-up: hold the hub alert open while talking, add Hang up (#85)

* Pop-up: hold the hub alert open while talking, add Hang up

The hub closed the doorbell pop-up when its countdown ran out, even mid
conversation. While the mic is on the pop-up now posts {bdhAlert: 'hold'}
to the hub (release on mute), and a Hang up button stops the mic and asks
the hub to close the pop-up. Needs BlackDiamondHub #370.


* Test: wait for async postMessage before checking what the hub heard


* Test: restore test_popup_without_kiosk_has_sound_but_no_talk header


---------

Talk: kiosk callbacks in iframes, red talk button, popup talk + sound (#84)

* Talk: kiosk callbacks in iframes, red talk button, popup talk + sound

- Shared _talk_style/_talk_script partials for camera page and doorbell popup
- Listen for kiosk talk callbacks re-posted to nested frames (kiosk v1.4)
- Bigger 128px talk button, red when talking, pulsing ring while connecting
- Popup: speaker on by default, mic muted, bottom-centred talk button


* Bump to 2.6.0b12


---------

Popup settings: tell same-named HA instances apart (2.6.0b11) (#83)

Both hubs had two connections named 'Home Assistant', so the popup showed two
identical section headers and entity labels. When names collide, label by
site (then id).
Release 2.6.0b10 (talkback; b9 tag was taken by #80) (#82)

Popup picker: group entities by device via ha.get_registry; collapsible HA sections (#80)

The picker used ha.ws_commands, which needs the admin-only ha.ws grant, so the
broker refused it and every entity landed under 'No device'. Use the read-only
ha.registry op (bdh-sdk 0.38, now with areas) instead, and test against a
FakeBroker that enforces the manifest's permissions.

Each Home Assistant instance's section can now be collapsed; the choice is
remembered on the device.

Cover page with tapped tile until fullscreen lands (2.6.0b8) (#79)

Android WebView enters fullscreen in steps, briefly showing the grid and
the other tiles being stopped. The tapped card now goes position:fixed
over the viewport immediately; cleared on refusal or exit.

Keep admin replay players hidden in the grid (2.6.0b7) (#77)

* Keep admin replay players hidden in the grid (2.6.0b7)

.cam-card video { display:block } out-ranked the .cam-replay/.cam-still hide rule, so two empty replay <video>s sat over each live stream for signed-in users. Android WebView draws a play-button placeholder on them.


* Test: use the Protect path so admin replay markup renders


* Test: check rendered boxes, not own display


---------

Show a fresh poster when returning to a site tab (2.6.0b6) (#76)

Stopping a tile left it marked has-frame with its dead source attached, so
switching back to a tab showed a black/frozen video over the poster until the
new stream's first frames. Stopping now saves the tile's last frame as its
poster and hides the video until the restarted stream presents frames.

Log page vitals every 5 s for the display crash hunt (2.6.0b5) (#75)

Adds a 'vit' stream event (frame pacing percentiles, timer lateness, long
tasks / long animation frames, heap, DOM size, GPU context state) every 5 s
and per-stream decode cost every 10 s, plus a 'boot' event with device/GPU
facts, WebGL context-loss, CPU pressure and uncaught-error events. The steady
vit events also act as a heartbeat that pins when the page stopped running.

Open a site tab from ?site= (2.6.0b4) (#74)

?site=mercer_island (or an index) opens that tab on load, so automation
and bookmarks can pick a site. Unknown or hidden sites open the first tab.

Restore grid status badges; add test-only ?selfreport=1 (2.6.0b3) (#73)

Hiding the badges (b2) made no difference to dropped frames (16.2% vs
16.9-17.5%), so they're back. ?selfreport=1 logs per-10 s painted-frame
drops and rAF fps via diag/events, so the page can be measured when
loaded on its own, without the hub page around it.

Test: hide grid status badges (2.6.0b2) (#72)

A/B whether the translucent, pulsing LIVE badges over each tile cost the
UC-Display painted frames (17% dropped at 7 streams, rAF 43 fps).

Push event rail invalidations instead of polling (2.6.0b1) (#71)

* Push event rail invalidations instead of polling (2.6.0)

Events publish a coalesced cameras/events/changed on the bdh-sdk event bus
(at most once per 250 ms); admins subscribe via BDHPush.live and refresh
the rail on invalidation. Needs bdh-sdk 0.36.


* Release as 2.6.0b1 (beta) so Mercer Island tries it first


---------

Events rail: update incrementally instead of rebuilding every 30 s (2.5.15) (#70)

The rail re-fetched the last 24 h of events every 30 s and rebuilt every
row (button + lazy thumbnail). At Mercer Island (~600 events/day) that was
a ~350 ms main-thread long task every 30 s on the UC-Display21 wall
displays, independent of stream count; Sun Peaks (~9 events) showed none.

Now an unchanged response is skipped, and rows are kept by event id and
reconciled in place: new events are inserted at the top, expired ones
removed, and existing rows (and their decoded thumbnails) left alone.

Test-only camera selection: ?only=<stream names> (2.5.14) (#69)

Plays only the named grid tiles (stored in localStorage like ?streams=N so it
survives crash relaunches; ?only=all clears it) and reports it in telemetry,
to test whether a single stream can crash the wall display.

Stream diagnostics: frame-gap events and a test-only stream cap (2.5.13) (#68)

- Per-stream requestVideoFrameCallback gaps (>300 ms), resolution changes
  and main-thread rAF gaps, batched to a new diag/events/ endpoint every
  2 s so they survive a renderer crash.
- ?streams=N caps the grid streams (stored in localStorage; ?streams=all
  clears) for the display crash ramp test.
- Telemetry adds loss/NACK/PLI, jitter buffer, transport and recent events.
Drop hub-navbar offsets inside iframe; add layout guard test (#67)
feat: send page telemetry (heap, WebRTC decoder stats) to the hub (2.5.11) (#66)

fix: live tiles rendered below their posters (2.5.10) (#65)

A two-line {# #} comment in the card markup isn't a Django comment (they're
single-line only), so it rendered as text in each card and pushed the
video-stream down 48-72px while the absolutely-positioned poster stayed put.
Use {% comment %} and assert no '{#' leaks into the page.

Also demote the per-call 'Camera cache HIT' log to debug: the stream keeper
now calls get_protect_cameras every 10s.

Stream keeper registers Protect cameras without a page load (2.5.9) (#64)

After an app update the app and go2rtc restart with nothing registered,
and an already-open wall display never reloads, so go2rtc stayed empty
and every tile sat on 'connecting'. The keeper now seeds its wanted set
from the (cached) Protect camera list on every pass.

Fullscreen falls back to low-res on hi-res restart; doorbell popup poster (2.5.8) (#63)

- restartStream: a failed fullscreen high-res stream no longer stops the
  whole card. Low-res restarts at once and only the high-res retry waits
  for the backoff (it could leave fullscreen empty for up to 30 s after a
  go2rtc restart).
- stopStream clears a pending restart even when the stream is inactive.
- Opening fullscreen resets the high-res backoff.
- Doorbell popup: cached live still under the video, which stays hidden
  until it has presented real frames (no black while connecting). Cold
  cache warms in the background, never blocking the popup.

Inline cached posters so cards never flash black on load (2.5.7) (#62)

Soak black-frame spans were all 'poster-loading': the poster's own
request landed 0.3-0.6 s after the page, after the first frame was due.
Cached stills are now embedded as data URIs for the visible site, and
other sites' posters load eagerly instead of lazily so switching site
doesn't flash black either.

Keep decode heap from creeping into the OOM killer (2.5.6) (#61)

Scrub bursts decode Protect frames on top of a heap that glibc kept and
fragmented: the app's baseline crept from ~68 to ~106 MiB over a soak and a
scrub drag's ~30 MiB transient hit the 128 MiB limit. Fix glibc's mmap
threshold so big pixel blocks are returned on free, trim the heap when a
burst of decodes ends, and raise the container limit to 192 MiB.

Replay diagnostics trail (2.5.5) (#60)

Record a per-scrubber trail of media events, retries, swaps, play() rejections and chrome hides, and expose it via the stats hook as cameras.scrub so soaks can root-cause 'paused, rs=0, chrome hidden' replay states.

Bound snapshot decodes to stop cameras OOM kills (#58)

* Bound snapshot decodes to stop cameras OOM kills

Scrubbing fired many historical snapshot requests at once; each decoded the
~1.6 MB full-size frame and spawned an extra unbounded thread to re-decode it
for the other warm width. On top of the ~81 MiB idle baseline that hit the
128 MiB cgroup limit (kernel OOM kill 2026-11-16 18:51 UTC).

- One decode per frame: warm widths are cut from the same image, largest first.
- At most 2 decodes at a time (semaphore); no per-request warm threads.


* Keep pyproject line endings


* Show replay controls when a replay pauses behind hidden chrome

The soak caught paused replays with the scrubber hidden: hideChrome won't hide while paused, but nothing re-showed chrome that was already hidden when the video later paused.


---------

Fix clip OOM; recover stuck/stalled streams; no black frame on start (#56)

- Event clips: export to a disk cache under BDH_DATA_DIR and stream them
  (with Range support) instead of buffering whole MP4s in memory.  Opening
  events OOM-killed the 128 MiB container, which also restarted go2rtc.
- Player watchdog: restart a tile (backing off up to 30 s) that never
  starts, whose peer connection closed/failed, or whose decoded frame
  count stops moving while it shows LIVE.
- Keep the video invisible until it has presented real frames (poster
  shows meanwhile); reveal high-res only after its first real frame.
- Start a new tab's streams on the next tick; more stream state in the
  remote frame stats.

Report per-stream state to the hub remote (2.5.0) (#55)

Registers a bdh.stats provider (bdh-sdk 0.33+, no-op on older SDKs) so the
hub's remote 'frame state' command returns each tile's stream name, mode,
peer-connection state, card state and video readiness/frame counts. Used by
the display soak to check that tiles are live and decoding.

device_control.description: Lodge device controls (scenes, lights, blinds) via Home Assistant

versions.changelog:
Assistant tools for the blinds: list_blinds and set_blinds (2.4.0b1) (#16)

list_blinds reports each Shades-tab blind by floor (open/closed/% open/moving);
set_blinds opens, closes, stops or positions blinds named loosely: a blind,
room, floor, 'great room', 'all', or several. Request and names are normalised
the same way so device words on either side never stop a match.

Assistant tools: list and activate scenes (2.3.0b1) (#15)

list_scenes (read-only) and activate_scene for the hub's voice/chat
assistant, offered in every mode like the homepage scene shortcuts and
limited to the scenes the "Scenes to show" setting allows. Needs
bdh-sdk 0.46.

Controls: remove fireplace (moved to the Fireplace app) - 2.2.0b1 (#14)

The Napoleon fireplace now lives in its own app (bdh-app-fireplace, via
pynapoleon). Drop the Fireplace tab, its api/fireplace/* endpoints, the
fireplace.js/css assets, the fireplace homepage status/shortcut, and the
climate/number/select/media grants that only the fireplace card used.

Remove Gemstone Lights; it is its own app now (2.1.0b1) (#12)

Gemstone moved to bdh-app-gemstone. Controls drops the Gemstone tab, its
API routes, client, static assets and settings (gemstone_email /
gemstone_password), plus the pygemstone and aiohttp dependencies.

- Manifest: network none (HA goes via the broker), lifecycle always
  (live homepage status), memory 96 MB.
- Regression test: no gemstone tab, markup, assets or routes.
- HaClientTests install a stub bdh_sdk.ha provider: since hub #363 HA
  comes only from Settings, so the mocked-HTTP tests got None.

Controls: pin the tab bar to the top of the iframe (2.0.2) (#11)

The sticky tab bar kept top: 62px from when the app was drawn under the
hub navbar in-process. In the container the app is in an iframe below the
navbar, so the bar floated 62px down and the controls scrolled behind and
above it. Pin it at top: 0 and add a test that fails on navbar offsets.

Fireplace: read the registry via ha.registry instead of ha.ws (2.0.1) (#10)

The Fireplace tab used ha.ws_commands, which needs the admin-only ha.ws
grant, so it 502'd in the container. bdh-sdk 0.32's ha.get_registry goes
through the hub's read-only ha.registry op, covered by the manifest's
ha.read globs (Napoleon only has climate/light/number/select/switch).
Output to the card is unchanged.

Port to hub API 2 container model (2.0.0) (#9)

- Manifest: api_version 2, network outbound, lifecycle always, 128 MB,
  least-privilege ha.read/ha.call per domain/service, media.
- gemstone_password is a SECRET (bdh_sdk.secrets with legacy env fallback).
- Gemstone aiohttp session uses trust_env so HTTPS_PROXY is honoured.
- Broker refusals (PermissionDenied) degrade to 502 / hidden fireplaces.
- Tests against FakeBroker; README container section.
Use shared hub scroll hint (#7)

flights.name: Flights
flights.description: Track flights with FlightAware and get delay, gate and landing alerts

versions.changelog: Flights: progress bar on its own row above airports on phones (0.1.3b8) (#10)

Fix Flights layout on phones (0.1.3b7) (#9)

Bare 1fr grid tracks let the detail card widen the page past the screen. Use minmax(0,1fr), add a <=600px phone layout (stacked footer buttons, bottom-sheet add dialog, full-width toast) and a test that rejects bare fr tracks.
Label airport calls on the usage page instead of 'not made by this hub' (0.1.3b6) (#8)
Drop the monthly limit card from the usage page (0.1.3b5) (#7)

Real FlightAware usage, admin-only usage page, stop polling at touchdown (0.1.3b4) (#6)

- Read month-to-date usage from FlightAware /account/usage (cached 5 min, stale fallback)
- Spending limit is a CHOICE setting (\/5/10/20/50); enforced against real total
- Admin-only Settings > Flights usage page with per-kind breakdown and refresh
- Flights app shows no totals, only a 95% warning / limit reached / off banner
- Poll every 2 min on final approach; stop at touchdown

Remove FlightAware cost numbers from the UI (#5)

Drops the monthly spend in the header and the per-search cost hint.
The budget limit and the 'budget used up' warning are unchanged.

Drop landed flights 10 minutes after touchdown (#4)

Landed flights now expire 10 min after touchdown (was 3 h). The worker
also wakes at each flight's expiry so it is pruned on time.

Search airports by city or name, with type-ahead and home pre-fill (#3)

Bundled OurAirports list (offline, no AeroAPI cost). Route search accepts
city, airport name, IATA/ICAO or 'City (CODE)'. Destination pre-fills with
the hub's nearest major airport.

Show gate arrival time and poll every minute near landing (#2)

The card showed runway touchdown (est_on) while FlightAware shows gate
arrival (est_in), and polling stopped at touchdown and ran every 5 min in
the air, so the card lagged ('In air' after landing) and never saw the gate.

- Arrival labels use est_in (gate); 'Landing now' within 2 min of touchdown
- Poll every 60 s in the last 15 min and after touchdown until act_in
  (max 45 min); 'Taxiing to C10' / 'At gate C10 1:02 PM'

Frame 1.0.0b10: a play button on each TV; slideshow starts from the Art Store (#10)

versions.changelog: Tonight shows the schedule that owns tonight; Name first in the schedule editor (#25)

Autopilot: collapsible card and scrolling Events panel (#24)

Plan tab: Coming up timeline, Autopilot and Schedules (admins) (#23)

Adds an admin-only Plan tab with a merged Autopilot/schedule timeline, the Autopilot settings (moved out of hub Settings) and Gemstone timers grouped into schedules. Tonight shows the playing schedule to everyone.

Previews match the lights; count designs started elsewhere (#22)

b20: instant design delete/undo; show Custom/Guest word on phones (#21)

Delete took seconds: it waited for the cloud delete and a full reload of
the designs before the card went. Now the card goes and the Undo toast
shows straight away, the delete goes out behind it, and the card comes
back with an error if the delete fails. Undo is instant the same way.

Phones now show 'Custom'/'Guest' next to the house/person icon instead of
just the icon.

b19: Discard changes in Create, '(copy)' names, Custom tag and heart on every card (#20)

- Create: '↺ Discard changes' when editing a saved design restores the design (and folder)

Gemstone 0.1.0b18: delete user designs with undo, card redesign (#19)

Card ⋯ menu (and long press) with Edit / Edit a copy, favourite toggle and Delete for designs the user may delete; Create header delete button. Delete is immediate with an Undo toast (restore within 5 min). Managed folders and library copies are stock and can't be deleted; guests can delete only Guest designs. Cards tag Custom/Guest outside folder groups. Copies are named 'Name 2', 'Name 3'.

0.1.0b17: Autopilot off backstop, brightness never turns lights on, activity log (#18)

The hot tub stayed on past Autopilot's off time after it got a brightness
command in the evening. Three minutes after the off time the worker now turns
off any Autopilot controller still on (once a night, respecting keep-on-until).
The brightness slider skips controllers that are off. Every command is logged
with who sent it (admin/guest/app), last 300, admin-only at api/activity/.

b16: fitting-room Create, LIVE badge, slim preview brightness + no blink, drop Admin label (#16)

- New designs are 'Untitled' / 'Untitled (n)'; name editable inline.
- 'ON LIGHTS' badge -> 'LIVE'; slim strip dims with brightness (dimOf).
- Slim preview no longer blinks on the 30 s refresh.
- Tests for each of the above.
b15: grouped/capped patterns, recently played, strip colours, tidy titles, clean photo swap, still preview fix (#15)

b14: Create back button, unclipped animation ring, pinned bar on return (#14)

- Create view gets a Back button to Tonight.
- Animation tile selection ring is drawn inside the tile so the grid can't clip it; swatch row padded for its ring.
- Returning to Tonight re-checks the pinned bar (the observer only fires on change).
- Tests: rings drawn inside, every view has a back button, Tonight re-syncs the pinned bar, heroHidden.

b13: merge Patterns into Tonight (#13)

Tonight now holds favourites, an All patterns grid with sticky category
chips, and a collapsed Gemstone library (lazy-loaded). Pattern cards get a
heart toggle (new /api/fav/). A pinned now-playing bar appears when the hero
scrolls away; its thumbnail is cropped to every light via fitBox. Lights-off
is a dropdown. The Patterns page and search are removed; #patterns routes to

voice.name: Voice
voice.description: Wake word and voice assistant for the wall screens

versions.changelog:
Listen socket: app-level keepalive ping every 15 s (0.2.0b5) (#5)

Websocket pings stop at the hub's proxy, so a screen couldn't tell a live
listen socket from one whose app end was gone (e.g. after the voice
container was replaced). The app now sends {"type":"ping"} every 15 s and
announces it in hello ("ping": 15); kiosk 1.14 reconnects when they stop.
Older kiosks ignore unknown message types.

End the conversation when the person is done; follow-up wait 5 s (0.2.0b4) (#4)

A built-in end_conversation tool, handled by the voice app (never the gateway): the model says a short goodbye and calls it, and the conversation ends once the goodbye has played. Speaking again cancels it.
Fix NameError in config.load (_bool lost in 0.2.0b2); test the real load (0.2.0b3) (#3)
Assistant: ask when a request is ambiguous; know which room the screen is in (0.2.0b2) (#2)

Voice assistant: Azure OpenAI Realtime conversations after the wake word (#1)

After a wake the listen socket carries a speech-to-speech conversation:
mic audio is upsampled to 24 kHz and streamed to the Realtime GA API, tool
calls run through the hub tools gateway, and reply audio streams back to the
screen as binary frames framed by speak_start/speak_end, with state and
transcript messages, barge-in, follow-up and max-length limits, and per-turn
records on voice/conversation. New settings: enabled, api_key (secret),
endpoint, model, voice, max_seconds, follow_up_seconds, instructions.
Needs the tools permission. Version 0.2.0b1.

Voice: wake-word detection for the wall screens (0.1.0b1)

Kiosks stream 16 kHz PCM to /voice/api/listen; openWakeWord's models run
with onnxruntime + numpy (scores identical to openwakeword 0.6.0) and the
app answers hello/wake/config JSON. Admin-only Settings -> Voice page with
connected screens and the last 50 detections with their clips.
